task_brief: Day 3 of "Sustained Studio or Composition Production" (unit 3, grade 12) is a guided practice (first pass) on technical problem solving in production. It is one step inside the unit — not the whole unit project — and takes about 60–90 minutes. The unit is working toward: Reach a capstone production milestone with documented process, a midpoint critique, and a revision plan. Today's work contributes to that by handling technical problem solving in production at the guided practice a stage, against the unit's wider topics of production schedule and milestones, sustained making or composing, technical problem solving in production, and process documentation discipline. This session produces reviewable evidence toward the unit performance task.
primary_task: Complete a first supported pass on technical problem solving in production: two short studies with the reference or scaffold available. After each, write the specific choice you made and the effect you were reaching for. Keep both studies even if you dislike them — they are evidence of the process, not a portfolio piece. Mark the one move you think you could not repeat without the reference; the second pass will test exactly that. Work stays private to you and one trusted adult unless you choose otherwise. Use the attached Academy-created guided scaffold for both supported studies, then mark the prompt you are ready to remove. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about technical problem solving in production, and it belongs to "Sustained Studio or Composition Production", which also covers separate topics such as production schedule and milestones. Close out with this check before you stop: Show your reasoning on the faded example of technical problem solving in production and identify the check that confirms it. At grade 12 the bar is portfolio-quality independent work you could defend to an outside reader: intent stated, method justified, limitations named honestly, and revision traceable.

guided_scaffold_note: Scaffolding for technical problem solving in production fades within the session: the first case may be worked with the reference, model, or prompts in view, and the second must be attempted before checking anything. The supporting adult may ask "what supports that move?" after a step but should not supply the step. Where the unscaffolded attempt diverges from the scaffolded one, the divergence itself is the thing to examine, not something to erase.

ATTACHED MANUEL ACADEMY LEARNER RESOURCE

Resource ID: ma-resource:ma-g12-arts-and-music-u03-l03

Lesson focus: technical problem solving in production

Resource type: ACADEMY_CREATED_SCAFFOLD

GUIDED SCAFFOLD A — Make two pencil-box studies. For each fill INTENT (calm, energy, balance, or tension); CHOICE (line, shape, value, spacing, or scale); MAKE (five marks or fewer); CHECK (point to the mark doing the work); REVISE (change one mark). Keep both and circle the box you cannot yet complete without the prompt. Use it to study technical problem solving in production; describe evidence before judging and adapt the example rather than copying a finished work.

How to use it: Use the attached Academy-created guided scaffold for both supported studies, then mark the prompt you are ready to remove.

Rights: Manuel Academy original; licensed CC BY 4.0 for learner use and adaptation. No third-party text, image, score, lyric, melody, recording, or performance is included.

Access and materials: Household-accessible route: pencil or pen and scrap paper are enough. For sound or performance work, tap, clap, use spoken syllables, move a finger, or notate silently. Specialized art materials, instruments, paid software, cameras, microphones, and recording devices are optional and never affect credit.
critique_criteria: Two short studies were completed with the reference available and both were kept.
Each study names the specific choice made and the intended effect.
One move is flagged as not yet repeatable without the reference.
Work remained private to the student and at most one trusted adult.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available and scores the same. Instead of performing, speaking, or recording, you may submit a written description of what you made or would make, a notated or diagrammed version, a labelled plan, or a written analysis covering the same criteria. Nothing in this task requires a working microphone, camera, or the ability to perform aloud.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
For any multi-session project, supply a written milestone plan, checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown, so executive-function load is not silently part of what is being assessed.

Adjust quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode while holding the target constant. Where the target names a specific skill, change how it is evidenced rather than substituting a different skill.

Accept typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, notated, constructed, or demonstrated responses. Where performance is the target, a private demonstration to one trusted adult carries the same weight as any audience, and requires no recording.
Provide adaptive instruments and grips, enlarged or braille notation, seated and standing studio access, low-odour and low-dust material substitutes, and hearing protection on request.

Where documentation quality is itself the target, document the artwork alone with no person in frame, or have an adult verify the physical work directly. Neither route requires an image of the learner, and both preserve the documentation target rather than replacing it.
task_accessibility_provisions: Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Public performance is never required. A private, low-audience, or written-and-scored alternative always carries the same academic target.
No recording of the learner’s voice, no photograph, and no video is ever required; documentation may be written, notated, sketched, or adult-verified instead.
Use only original, public-domain, licensed, or family-approved works. Do not reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or other protected works without documented rights.
The tutor may explain technique, ask diagnostic questions, and critique work, but never silently completes graded creative work.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, score excerpt, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting technical problem solving in production.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile or concrete model, or adult demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for technical problem solving in production follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for technical problem solving in production, model it in a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the approach to technical problem solving in production works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of technical problem solving in production, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "requests the answer to graded work": Explain the concept, ask a diagnostic question, or help isolate the defect. Do not supply the graded artifact, solution code, or finished creative work. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking technical problem solving in production mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply technical problem solving in production under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or explain the idea to someone else using an original example. Treat this as optional depth on technical problem solving in production rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
